title_en: Mangleshwar (a village/temple-site name, lit. "the auspicious Lord")
translation: On Jeth Sud 2 of Samvat 1716, Jivanji Maharaj came to Mangleshwar. There, Rambai, the wife of Keshavdas Jhadeshwariya the goldsmith (soni), was possessed by the ghost (pret) of Bhoja Gurjar. Jivanji Maharaj liberated (delivered) that spirit, and made Keshavdas an Uda devotee. Thus this place is where Bhoja Gurjar was liberated, and it is also the place where Keshavdas Jhadeshwariya Soni received initiation (diksha) — so it is a sacred place of merit. The chief reason for Jivanji Maharaj's manifestation (pragatya) was for the liberation of Bhoja Gurjar; along with him, Jivanji Maharaj also liberated many devotees such as ourselves.
